calls.headline: The pound falls a sixth session to EGP 54.01 and the EGX30 adds 1% as foreigners buy
calls.body: The central bank sold the dollar at EGP 54.01 (buy 53.87) on Thursday against 54.77, down 1.4% on the day, 3.8% in November and 3.9% below its 52-week high of EGP 56.20. The EGX30 gained 0.99% to 51,152.73, up 22.3% this year and about 10% below its September peak, while the EGX70 EWI rose 2.4% to a 52-week high of 17,567. Foreign investors were net buyers of about EGP 0.21–0.22bn, Egyptians net sellers of about EGP 0.19bn, with Arab investors' side disputed between outlets (Masrawy, Youm7, Youlyou); turnover was EGP 9.5–10.2bn. The central bank sold 364-day bills at a weighted 26.03% and 182-day bills at 25.25%, slightly below the prior week's 26.08% and 25.46%, still about 12 points above 13.9% inflation.
calls.view: The wide real yield is still paying foreign money to stay, and a sixth easing in the dollar shows the carry trade working; with the 364-day yield barely lower, the pound has room toward EGP 53–54.5. The risk is the weekend: the exchange reopens Sunday after Wall Street's worst day since April 2025 and Asian tech selling, and Egypt's foreign buying is the first thing risk-off hits. Banks and the most liquid blue chips are the stocks that gain most from a firm pound.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before the end of November, or the EGX30 closes below 49,255.66 (Tuesday's low) on foreign selling.

calls.headline: Wall Street's tech rout meets an EGX that cannot trade until Sunday
calls.line: Egyptian stocks reopen Sunday after a 4.4% S&P 500 fall and 6% drops in Tokyo and Seoul; foreign money is the channel.
calls.body: The S&P 500 lost 4.36% to 7,353.73 and the Nasdaq 5.52% on Thursday, its worst day since April 2025, with the semiconductor index down about 12%; the Kospi and Nikkei closed about 6% lower on Friday and the Taiex 4.5% (CNN, Al Jazeera; closes differ by source). The Institute of International Finance estimated $33.8bn of emerging-market portfolio outflows in October. The EGX is shut Friday and Saturday, so none of this is in Thursday's prices.
calls.view: Egypt has little direct exposure to AI stocks, but foreign investors who bought Egyptian bills and shares this week can sell them to cover losses elsewhere; the first test is Sunday's foreign net flow. A softer dollar and cheaper oil from risk-off would offset part of it. Expect banks and the biggest foreign-owned names to move first.
calls.wrong: Foreign investors are net buyers again on Sunday and the EGX30 holds above 50,500.

calls.headline: Developers beat the EGX30 as Palm Hills jumps 5.7% and Emaar Misr awards an EGP 7.1bn contract
calls.line: After lagging all week, developers led Thursday, which weakens the case that dearer money keeps them behind.
calls.body: Palm Hills rose 5.7% to EGP 11.91, Elsewedy Electric 3.7% to EGP 116.11 and Talaat Moustafa 2.7% to EGP 83.25 while the EGX30 gained 1.0% (Asoul Misr). Emaar Misr contracted Innovo Construction for about EGP 7.1bn to build and finish 213 villas and townhouses on two Marassi Red parcels over 27 months (Eleqtisadenews, Mubasher). Talaat Moustafa's EGP 970bn North Coast project announced in October remains without disclosed terms.
calls.view: Thursday's jump is one session against a month of lag, and the hike still raises buyers' installment costs; but contractors and cable makers (Elsewedy) win from the building that developers keep awarding. Treat it as a rotation toward real assets in a firm-pound week, not a break in the rate story.
calls.wrong: Palm Hills closes above EGP 12.50 or Talaat Moustafa above EGP 88.

calls.headline: Telecom Egypt guides low double-digit growth for 2027 as its shares near double
calls.line: A steady outlook after a 95.5% rise this year leaves the stock priced for delivery, not surprise.
calls.body: Telecom Egypt's board approved a 2027 budget with low double-digit revenue growth, an EBITDA margin in the low-to-mid 40s and an in-service capex-to-sales ratio in the mid-20s (Telecompaper, Zawya). The stock rose 0.4% to EGP 128.55, a fourth gain, up 95.5% this year. It reported profit growth of 46.3% for the nine months (Twasl, reported).
calls.view: Guidance of low double-digit growth sits close to Egypt's inflation, meaning real growth is modest; the stock's rise already reflects a re-rating, so further gains need earnings or dividends to beat the budget. Medium-term support: capex discipline and a wide dollar-linked cable business.
calls.wrong: Telecom Egypt closes below EGP 115 (about 10% below Thursday) before its next results.

calls.headline: The Nasdaq falls 5.5% into a correction as chip stocks suffer their worst day since March 2020
calls.body: The S&P 500 lost 4.36% to 7,353.73, the Nasdaq 5.52% to 24,315.00 and the Dow 3.44% to 51,523.06, a drop of about 1,833 points; the S&P 500 and Nasdaq had their worst days since April 2025 and the Nasdaq is more than 10% below its October 6 record. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 12.3%. Nvidia dropped 8.9% to $182.29, Broadcom 10.2%, Tesla 10.7%, Sandisk 22%; Treasury yields were slightly lower. Investors pointed to Democratic gains that could tighten oversight of AI data centers, weak results from Arm and Qualcomm and doubts about AI returns (CNN, NBC News, The National).
calls.view: This is positioning, not a verdict on demand: Wednesday's record highs left chips crowded, and the political news gave holders a reason to cut. Strategist Ed Yardeni calls it a bubble 'losing some air' rather than bursting. Friday's payrolls and Asia's open decide whether this is a one-day flush or the start of a longer slide; the first sign of stabilization would be chips rising on Friday's open.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes back above 25,736.51 (Wednesday's close) by November 13, or Nvidia above $220.

calls.headline: Voters' rejection of data centers hits Meta, Oracle and the AI build-out
calls.line: Meta warned that backlash after the midterms could slow AI expansion, and voters rejected data-center measures in 39 of 40 ballot questions.
calls.body: Meta warned that voter opposition to data centers could make expanding AI infrastructure harder (TechCrunch); Meta fell 3.6% to $607.17 and Oracle 6.9% to $115.19, now 40.9% lower this year (TIKR: 'Washington is the new worry'). Microsoft was reported to have abandoned a Texas contract extension with Nscale and Microsoft's neocloud deliveries are slipping, per MarketScreener and Euronext news (reported, not confirmed by Microsoft).
calls.view: Permits and local approvals raise the cost and delay the timing of capacity that investors had priced in as certain; the winners are firms with power and sites already secured. This supports the desk's view that spenders trade below steadier earners until returns show up.
calls.wrong: A large data-center project clears local approval and the stocks rebound above Wednesday's levels.

calls.headline: A Fed rate rise stays on the table as the Bank of England hikes to 4% before payrolls
calls.line: Payrolls at 3:30pm decide how many hike bets survive the rout.
calls.body: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4%, its first hike since August 2023, in an 8-1 vote; Catherine Mann wanted 50. Traders cut bets on a Federal Reserve rate rise on December 8–9 to about 60%. US October payrolls are due at 3:30pm Cairo time on Friday. The dollar index edged up 0.1% to 101.57, within 1% of its 52-week high.
calls.view: A strong jobs figure keeps the hike odds alive and pressures both stocks and emerging-market currencies; a weak one lifts bonds and eases the squeeze on growth stocks. The market has already repriced equities, so the bigger risk is a hot number into an already fragile tape.
calls.wrong: Payrolls come in far below consensus yet stocks keep falling, which would show the sell-off is about AI, not rates.

calls.headline: Brent rises 3.9% to $98.29 as Iran exempts four countries' ships from Hormuz limits
calls.line: Oil bounced from Wednesday's 9% fall while Exxon fell with the market.
calls.body: Brent rose 3.9% to $98.29, still 13.3% below its level at the start of the month; Exxon Mobil fell 2.1% to $165.79. A senior Iranian lawmaker said ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar may cross Hormuz freely, while the US blockade of Iranian ports remains (Al Jazeera). More than 120 commercial ships have been hit since the war began on February 28.
calls.view: The exemptions change little for supply now; oil is trading on talk of a settlement, which keeps it between $90 and $105. Exxon's decline with the market shows it is not behaving as a hedge on a risk-off day.
calls.wrong: Brent closes above $105, which would reverse the settlement hopes.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: November's 100 bps hike raises what banks earn on loans and T-bills faster than their deposit costs; CIB closed up a fourth session at EGP 128.00 and EFG Holding rose 1.2% to EGP 23.78, both still below their 50-day averages.

sectors.why: Banque du Caire’s retail tranche was 27 times covered and the state plans to list Enppi in January: more offerings mean more fees and more trading.

sectors.name: Dollar earners: contractors, cables, fertilizers
sectors.why: The dollar is 8% higher against the pound in a month, which lifts the pound value of export and overseas revenue at Orascom, Elsewedy and Abu Qir.

stocks.why: A return to its 50-day average (about 130). The hike widens margins, and CIB rose 1.2% to EGP 128.00 on Thursday, 6.2% above its EGP 120.47 start on October 30 and within the projected range's floor; it is still about 11% below its 52-week high.
stocks.wrong: it closes below EGP 114, 5% under Thursday’s close, or the EGX30 falls while it does.

stocks.why: Dollar revenue from Gulf and US projects; Orascom rose 1.6% to EGP 810.02, still below its EGP 822 start, and it is up 88.4% this year. A stronger pound trims translation gains, so a pause is as likely as a new high.
stocks.wrong: it closes below EGP 780, 5% under Thursday, or the pound recovers sharply.

sectors.name: Real estate developers
sectors.why: Dearer financing hits installment buyers and developers' own borrowing at once, but Palm Hills and Talaat Moustafa outperformed on Thursday (+5.7% and +2.7%) and Emaar Misr is still awarding contracts; confidence stays medium only because they remain below their 50-day averages.

sectors.name: Food and consumer
sectors.why: A weaker pound raises the cost of imported inputs such as milk powder and packaging; companies with pricing power, like Juhayna, pass it on with a lag.

stocks.why: Up 2.7% to EGP 83.25 on Thursday, 3.5% above its EGP 80.40 start and ahead of the EGX30's 3.1%, so the call is currently going against the desk; the hike lands on its buyers and its debt and its state deals are long-term offsets, so confidence is low.
stocks.wrong: it closes back above EGP 88, near its 50-day average, or a big sales launch beats expectations.

stocks.why: Jumped 5.7% to EGP 11.91 on Thursday, 4.5% above its EGP 11.40 start and beyond the EGX30's move, under the same rate pressure as Talaat Moustafa. Al Ahly Pharos values it at EGP 21.40 on existing assets alone, which argues against a deep fall.

egp.finding: The central bank sold the dollar at EGP 54.01 on Thursday, down for a sixth session from EGP 54.77 and the lowest in at least a year, 3.8% lower in November; the 364-day bill cleared at 26.03% and the 182-day at 25.25%, slightly below the previous week, about 12 points above September's 13.9% inflation.

drivers.name: Rates raised 100 bps
drivers.why: Deposit 20.00%, lending 21.00% from November 1. Thursday's auction cleared the 364-day bill at 26.03% (26.08% the week before) and the 182-day at 25.25% (25.46%): demand held with a slightly lower yield, which suggests foreign money is still arriving. Net international reserves rose to $57.5bn in October from $57.35bn.

drivers.name: Oil rebounds to $98
drivers.why: Brent rose 3.9% to $98.29 on Thursday but is 13.3% below its level at the start of the month; Goldman Sachs still sees $105 by December, and Iran's exemptions for four countries' ships leave supply little changed.

drivers.name: Remittances up 27.2%
drivers.why: Remittances from Egyptians abroad rose to $33.9bn in the first eight months of 2026, a major dollar source that supports the pound (Daily News Egypt, citing central bank data).

drivers.name: IMF eighth and final review
drivers.why: The program expires on December 15 and state offerings are among its requirements. A passed review steadies inflows; a delay would weigh on the pound. Global risk-off after Thursday's Wall Street rout is the new test of foreign appetite.

view.headline: A sixth easing and a wide real yield keep the dollar in EGP 53–54.5, but risk-off is the test
view.body: The central bank's rate fell to EGP 54.01 on Thursday, a sixth straight easing and 3.6% below October 30's EGP 56.04. With the one-year bill at 26.03% and September inflation at 13.9%, the real yield stays wide enough to pay foreign holders to stay. The risk is the emerging-market outflow a global sell-off can start; the October outflow was $33.8bn (IIF).
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before the end of November, or the next auction's average yield falls sharply.
